definitions.gloss: broad daylight; the middle of the day
definitions.explanation: Daytime, especially thought of as bright and fully public. The word is almost always used to draw attention to something unusual happening when it would normally not — typically a crime, bold act, or strange incident that occurs in full public view rather than under cover of darkness.

examples.japanese: {白昼|はくちゅう}{堂々|どうどう}と{犯行|はんこう}におよんだ。
examples.english: He committed the crime in broad daylight and without hesitation.

examples.japanese: {白昼|はくちゅう}の{繁華街|はんかがい}で{事件|じけん}が{起|お}きた。
examples.english: The incident occurred in a busy downtown area in broad daylight.

examples.japanese: {白昼|はくちゅう}に{銀行|ぎんこう}が{襲|おそ}われるという{大胆|だいたん}な{事件|じけん}が{報道|ほうどう}された。
examples.english: A bold incident in which a bank was robbed in broad daylight was reported in the news.

notes:
Composed of {白|はく} (white, bright) and {昼|ちゅう} (daytime). Literally "bright day." Although the dictionary meaning is simply "daytime," in actual use the word carries a strong nuance of "in plain view, when everyone can see," and is overwhelmingly attached to crimes, shocking incidents, or brazen acts. It is a written / news-register word; everyday conversation uses {昼間|ひるま}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {白昼|はくちゅう}{堂々|どうどう}: in broad daylight, brazenly
- {白昼|はくちゅう}{夢|む}: daydream
- {白昼|はくちゅう}の{犯行|はんこう}: a crime committed in broad daylight
- {白昼|はくちゅう}の{街|まち}: the city by daylight
- {白昼|はくちゅう}に{及|およ}ぶ: (typically of a crime) to take place in broad daylight

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {昼間|ひるま}: daytime — the neutral everyday word; no nuance of shocking exposure
- {真昼|まひる}: high noon, midday — emphasizes the middle of the day; more literary but less crime-associated
- {日中|にっちゅう}: during the day — factual, often used in forecasts and schedules
- {昼日中|ひるひなか}: broad daylight — old-fashioned, similar nuance to {白昼|はくちゅう} but rarer
